findings.before: The instrument once sounded because strings and player worked together. Now both conditions are withdrawn: its strings are broken and its players have gone. The second line refuses to treat the remaining object as self-sufficient. Read in the surrounding reflections on body, loss and remembrance, the instrument offers a way to attend to mortality without pretending the body commands its own continuance. The image does not specify an anatomical counterpart for every string. Its force lies in the silence after animation has ceased.
findings.after: The two lines remove both the strings and the players that once made the instrument sound. The remaining instrument cannot continue by itself. This image can prompt reflection on mortality, but that application is not the only reading. Another interpretation takes the instrument as bodily attachment and its silence as release from that attachment. The surrounding call to remain absorbed in Ram makes this possibility relevant. Keep the image intact while asking whether its ending describes the loss of life or the ending of an attachment within life.

findings.before: The decisive words are leaving remembrance. They distinguish this warning from a general rejection of family life. The speaker may devote great energy to maintaining a household and still fail to secure what endures. The intimate address brother brings the warning close rather than presenting a remote example. The final bond or support cannot simply be assumed from the size of the family. The Salok asks what accompanies the work of caring, and what is lost when Hari disappears from its centre.
findings.after: The decisive opening is leaving Hari's remembrance. It distinguishes the warning from a rejection of caring for a family. The household may receive all one's attention, yet brothers and kin cannot supply the enduring support that has been neglected. This family reading gives the final words a direct connection with the opening household. The exact force of being left in one's affairs remains interpretive. What is clear is the imbalance: care has become absorbing occupation while remembrance, which should accompany it, has been abandoned.

findings.after: ਨਿਰਣਾਇਕ ਸ਼ੁਰੂਆਤ ਹਰਿ ਦਾ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਛੱਡਣਾ ਹੈ। ਇਸ ਨਾਲ ਚੇਤਾਵਨੀ ਪਰਿਵਾਰ ਦੀ ਸੰਭਾਲ ਦੇ ਇਨਕਾਰ ਤੋਂ ਵੱਖ ਹੁੰਦੀ ਹੈ। ਸਾਰਾ ਧਿਆਨ ਕੁਟੰਬ ਉੱਤੇ ਲੱਗ ਸਕਦਾ ਹੈ, ਪਰ ਭਾਈ-ਬੰਧ ਉਸ ਟਿਕਾਊ ਆਸਰੇ ਦੀ ਥਾਂ ਨਹੀਂ ਲੈ ਸਕਦੇ ਜਿਸ ਨੂੰ ਭੁਲਾ ਦਿੱਤਾ। ਰਿਸ਼ਤੇਦਾਰਾਂ ਵਾਲੀ ਪੜ੍ਹਤ ਅੰਤਲੇ ਬੋਲਾਂ ਨੂੰ ਪਹਿਲੀ ਤੁਕ ਦੇ ਕੁਟੰਬ ਨਾਲ ਸਿੱਧਾ ਜੋੜਦੀ ਹੈ। ਧੰਧਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਰਹਿ ਜਾਣ ਦੀ ਠੀਕ ਅੰਤਲੀ ਹਾਲਤ ਹਾਲੇ ਭਾਵਾਰਥ ਮੰਗਦੀ ਹੈ। ਸਪਸ਼ਟ ਗੱਲ ਅਸੰਤੁਲਨ ਹੈ: ਸੰਭਾਲ ਪੂਰੀ ਤਰ੍ਹਾਂ ਰੁਝੇਵਿਆਂ ਵਿੱਚ ਡੁੱਬਣਾ ਬਣੀ ਅਤੇ ਨਾਲ ਚੱਲਣ ਵਾਲਾ ਸਿਮਰਨ ਛੱਡਿਆ ਗਿਆ।

findings.before: The first line gives wisdom a centre: Hari remembered in the heart. The second supplies a striking contrast, someone playing where a fall has no safe landing. Skill alone cannot remove the danger created by that position. Read after the warnings about substitute rites, the image questions reliance upon clever arrangements that leave the deeper problem untouched. Remembrance is not presented as one more trick among them. It changes the basis on which the seeker stands and the meaning of being wise.
findings.after: The first line calls remembrance of Hari the highest wisdom. The next image does not make that wisdom effortless: playing upon a stake is demanding, and falling offers no secure resting place. Read together, the lines join a clear spiritual aim with the seriousness of remaining faithful to it. This is the relation emphasized in Sahib Singh's interpretation. The draft should therefore avoid assigning the stake confidently to worldly cleverness. The disturbing image belongs to the passage's account of remembrance, not to a physical practice to perform.

findings.before: The opening question challenges a sleep in which spiritual urgency has disappeared. The grave in the second line supplies the reason this comfort is misplaced. Kabir is not describing a distant exception that happens only to others; the coming dwelling belongs to the person addressed. Fear and grief therefore enter the poem as an interruption of complacency. The Salok's force lies in waking before the end, while response is still possible. The following verses give that wakefulness a direction through remembrance and renewed union.
findings.after: The grave answers the opening question: a person whose life will end cannot take unawareness as lasting security. The call to awaken is clear, while the phrase about weeping, fear and suffering is compressed. It may be heard as grief interrupting complacency, or read idiomatically as leaving worldly fears and sorrows behind. Neither application should obscure the movement toward wakefulness. The following Saloks make its direction clearer through remembering Murari and returning to the One from whom the person has become separated.

The speaker is not simply celebrating a larger following. The fragrance image makes influence arise from what has inwardly developed, while the final name prevents the attention from ending with the admired devotee. Read beside earlier criticism of gathering disciples without befriending Keso, this Salok distinguishes attraction rooted in devotion from influence that replaces devotion with its own importance.
findings.after: Musk and bees provide an image of fragrance and attraction. The second line links that attraction with devotion and Ram's abiding. These readings differ, but both keep devotion and Divine abiding at the centre. The simple lines above follow the poet-reference reading provisionally; the alternative should remain visible until the grammar and theology receive qualified review.
